questions.question: What are Optional and Union types in Python, and when do you use them?
questions.title: Optional and Union Types in Python
questions.direct_answer: Optional[X] means 'X or None' — a value that might be absent (e.g., a user not found). Union[X, Y] means 'X or Y' — a value of one of several types (e.g., an id that's int or str). Since Python 3.10, you write these with the pipe: X | None and X | Y, which are shorter and preferred. Use Optional when a value can be missing (a nullable field, a maybe-not-found result), and Union when a value can legitimately be one of several types. mypy checks that you handle None (narrow the type) and that operations are valid for all members of a union.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you understand Optional as X-or-None (nullable) and Union as X-or-Y (one of several types), and the modern X | None / X | Y syntax.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Confusing Optional (nullable) with a default of None, or returning Optional without handling the None case (mypy flags it).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Optional[X] = X or None (nullable); Union[X,Y] = X or Y. Modern syntax: X | None, X | Y (3.10+). mypy makes you handle None (narrow) and check union members.

sections.title: Nullable and Multi-Type Values
sections.content: Optional[X] means 'X or None' — a value that might be absent, like a user that wasn't found. Union[X, Y] means 'X or Y' — a value that can be one of several types, like an id that's an int or a str. Since Python 3.10, you write these with the pipe operator: X | None and X | Y, which are shorter and now preferred over typing.Optional/typing.Union. Use Optional when a value can be missing (a nullable field, a maybe-not-found result) and Union when a value can legitimately be one of several types. mypy enforces that you handle the None case (narrow the Optional before using it) and that any operation is valid for all members of a union (or you narrow with isinstance).

sections.title: Optional vs Union
sections.content:
Optional adds None as a possibility; Union lists several types. The pipe syntax (3.10+) is preferred.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  O[X \| None] -->|nullable| N[may be None]
  U[X \| Y] -->|one of| M[multi-type]
  N -->|narrow with| C[if x is None: ...]
  M -->|narrow with| I[isinstance check]
```

sections.title: Optional and Union in practice
sections.content:
```python
# (1) OPTIONAL: a value that might be None (nullable).
def find_user(id: int) -> User | None:        # 3.10+ (was Optional[User])
    if id in self.users: return self.users[id]
    return None                               # might not be found

u = find_user(7)
if u is not None:                              # mypy NARROWS: u is User here
    print(u.name)                              # safe — mypy knows u isn't None

# (2) UNION: a value of one of several types.
def get_id(record: dict) -> int | str:        # 3.10+ (was Union[int, str])
    return record.get("id", "unknown")

rid = get_id(rec)
if isinstance(rid, int):                       # narrow the union
    total += rid                               # safe — mypy knows it's int
else:
    print(rid)                                # str here
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Confusing Optional (nullable) with a parameter that defaults to None — they're related but distinct.
Returning Optional[X] but using it without checking for None — mypy flags the unsafe access.
Operating on a Union without narrowing (isinstance) — an operation may not exist on all members.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Optional[X] = X or None (nullable); Union[X, Y] = X or Y (one of several types).
Modern syntax (3.10+): X | None and X | Y — shorter and preferred over typing.Optional/Union.
Use Optional for nullable/maybe-absent values; Union for values of one of several types.
mypy makes you handle None (narrow with `if x is None`) before using an Optional.
For a Union, narrow with isinstance before operations that aren't valid on all members.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: Optional of X means X or None — a value that might be absent, like a user that wasn't found. Union of X and Y means X or Y — a value that can be one of several types, like an id that's an int or a str. Since Python 3.10, you write these with the pipe operator: X pipe None and X pipe Y, which are shorter and now preferred over typing.Optional and typing.Union. Use Optional when a value can be missing — a nullable field, a maybe-not-found result — and Union when a value can legitimately be one of several types. mypy enforces that you handle the None case by narrowing the Optional before using it, and that any operation is valid for all members of a union, or you narrow with isinstance. The common mistakes are confusing Optional, which is nullable, with a parameter that defaults to None — they're related but distinct — returning Optional of X but using it without checking for None, which mypy flags as an unsafe access, and operating on a Union without narrowing with isinstance, because an operation may not exist on all members.
